advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the ticket dir name in `_first_in_progress_ns` via `resolve_ticket_dir_name(ticket_id, tracker)` instead of joining the raw `ticket_id`, matching the sidecar read idiom.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/completion.py:253: `ticket_dir = _os.path.join(str(_config.tracker_dir(repo_root)), ticket_id)`

`_ids.py:286-290` documents this exact anti-pattern: "Read sites that build a filesystem path from a ticket id use this [resolve_ticket_dir_name] in place of the unsafe ``resolve_ticket_id(id) or id`` idiom, which resurrected the raw (possibly traversing) id whenever resolution failed."
completion_sidecar.py:119 uses the safe idiom: `rid = resolve_ticket_dir_name(ticket_id, tracker); ticket_dir = os.path.join(tracker, rid)`
`_ids.resolve_ticket_id` (src/rebar/_ids.py:244-268) shows dir names can be aliases or 4+char prefixes distinct from the full ticket id
advisory.finding: `_first_in_progress_ns` builds the on-disk ticket directory by directly joining the raw `ticket_id` (`os.path.join(tracker_dir, ticket_id)`) instead of resolving it via `resolve_ticket_dir_name`, the idiom every other read site in the codebase uses. When the passed id is not byte-identical to the tracker dir name (an alias, a prefix/short id, or a Jira key — all resolvable ids per `_ids.resolve_ticket_id`), `os.path.isdir` returns False and the function silently returns `None`, causing `epic_bug_candidates` to fall back to the epic's `created_at` anchor — a wider window that over-includes candidates rather than using the intended first-claim anchor.
scenarios: An epic close where `canonical` (the compiled ticket_id) differs from the tracker dir name, or any future caller that passes an alias/prefix — the anchor silently degrades to created_at.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the raw join with the resolver used elsewhere: `rid = resolve_ticket_dir_name(ticket_id, str(_config.tracker_dir(repo_root)))` inside a try that returns None on FileNotFoundError, then `ticket_dir = os.path.join(tracker, rid)`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Compute the epic subtree states once per close and thread them (or the titles) into the candidate filter and screen instead of re-walking in `run_screen`.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/epic_bug_screen.py:251: `for s in completion._epic_subtree_states(epic_id, repo_root)[1:]` — a full re-walk just for titles
src/rebar/llm/completion.py:330: `states = _epic_subtree_states(ticket_id, repo_root)` inside `epic_bug_candidates`
src/rebar/llm/completion.py:280-282: `epic_bug_floor_findings` also calls `_epic_subtree_states`
_epic_subtree_states issues one `_reads.list_tickets(parent=pid, ...)` per node (completion.py:221)
advisory.finding: The epic subtree BFS (`_epic_subtree_states`, which re-lists children of every node) runs multiple times per epic close: once inside `epic_bug_floor_findings` (gate_ops floor arm), once inside `epic_bug_candidates`, and again directly in `run_screen` to build `children_titles`. Each walk re-issues `list_tickets(parent=...)` per subtree node, so a deep/wide epic pays the full descendant enumeration 3+ times per close.
scenarios: Closing an epic with a large descendant subtree — the store is walked redundantly, and `_open_bugs` (a full store scan of open+in_progress bugs) is likewise repeated across the floor and candidate stages.

evidence: gate_ops.py:84-106 `try: floor = epic_bug_floor_findings(...) except Exception as exc: ... uncertified = list(uncertified) + [{...'could not be read'...}]`

search over tests/unit/test_epic_bug_screen_4b54.py for 'withhold' and over tests/ for 'floor read' returned no matches; the mirrored arm's test test_child_enumeration_read_error_withholds_certification exists at tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_verification_workflow.py:217 but covers child_closure_findings, not epic_bug_floor_findings
advisory.finding: The epic-close caused_by floor READ-ERROR arm in completion_precheck (gate_ops.py:84-106) is untested: when epic_bug_floor_findings raises, the contract is never-block, never-crash, and WITHHOLD certification via a specific 'could not be read' finding. No test exercises this branch, even though the parallel child-closure read-error arm it explicitly mirrors HAS a dedicated regression test (test_child_enumeration_read_error_withholds_certification). advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that monkeypatches completion.epic_bug_floor_findings to raise inside completion_precheck for an epic with a passing child gate, then asserts run_verify is True, verdict is not FAIL from the floor, and certifiable is False with the 'could not be read' criterion present.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Memoize `_epic_subtree_states` (compute once per close and share across floor/candidate-filter/children_titles) and stop re-walking the whole store per subtree node — e.g. reduce the store once and traverse parent links in-memory, or list children by a single parent-indexed pass.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/completion.py:221 `for child in _reads.list_tickets(parent=pid, repo_root=repo_root):` inside the BFS `while frontier` loop — one list_tickets call per subtree node

list_tickets -> list_by_query -> list_states -> `reduce_all_tickets(tracker, ...)` at src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:384, which `os.listdir(tracker_path)` and `reduce_ticket(entry_path)` for EVERY ticket dir (src/rebar/reducer/_api.py:247-268) — a full-store O(N) walk per call regardless of the `parent=` filter
Called 3× per close with no caching: completion.py:281 (epic_bug_floor_findings), completion.py:330 (epic_bug_candidates), epic_bug_screen.py:251 (children_titles)
Baseline `child_closure_findings` only did ONE `list_tickets(parent=...)` (direct children); this change replaces that with an unbounded-depth BFS repeated three times
advisory.finding: `_epic_subtree_states` issues one full-store reduction (`reduce_all_tickets`, which walks/reduces every ticket dir in the tracker) per subtree node in its BFS, and is called 3 separate times per epic close (floor, candidate filter, children_titles) with no memoization — total store-read cost is O(subtree_size × total_ticket_count) per close.
scenarios: A large repository with a deep/wide epic subtree (many descendants) and a large total ticket store: closing one epic performs subtree_size × store_size ticket reductions × 3
Deep hierarchies where the BFS frontier is large amplify the number of full-store walks
advisory.suggested_fix: Compute the subtree states once per epic close and pass the result to `epic_bug_floor_findings`, `epic_bug_candidates`, and the children_titles derivation. Additionally, avoid per-node full-store reductions: reduce all tickets once and build a parent->children index in memory for the BFS instead of one `list_tickets(parent=pid)` (full-store) call per node.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate open/in_progress bugs once per epic close and share the result between the caused_by floor and the candidate filter instead of re-reducing the whole store in each.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/completion.py:236-237 loops `for status in ('open','in_progress'): bugs.extend(_reads.list_tickets(status=status, ticket_type='bug', ...))` — 2 full-store reductions per call

Called at completion.py:284 (epic_bug_floor_findings) and completion.py:343 (epic_bug_candidates), both run in the same close path (gate_ops.py:85 floor, gate_ops.py:151 run_screen->epic_bug_candidates) with no shared/cached result
Each list_tickets -> `reduce_all_tickets` walks the entire tracker (src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:384)
advisory.finding: `_open_bugs` performs two full-store reductions (one per status: open, in_progress) and is invoked once in `epic_bug_floor_findings` and again in `epic_bug_candidates`, so an epic close does 4 full-store reductions just to enumerate open bugs — the enumeration cost scales with total ticket count and is duplicated rather than shared.
scenarios: Large ticket stores where reducing all tickets is expensive; every epic close redoes the full-store bug enumeration up to 4 times
advisory.suggested_fix: Compute `_open_bugs(repo_root)` once in the precheck and thread it into both `epic_bug_floor_findings` and `epic_bug_candidates`; optionally use a single `status` filter pass if the query layer supports OR-ing statuses.
